newsitem.title: FRANCE: French ministry contradicts Godfrain on Zaire.
newsitem.headline: French ministry contradicts Godfrain on Zaire.

text.p: The French foreign ministry, contradicting the country's minister in charge of African affairs, indicated on Sunday that Paris still favoured sending an international military force to Zaire.

"The Ministry of Foreign Affairs wishes to underline that France's position on the implementing of United Nations resolutions about Zaire has not changed, notably concerning the deployment of a multinational force," a two-paragraph communique said.
The ministry's press section was not immediately available for further comment on its statement.

But it was clearly a response to an interview published on Sunday in the weekly newspaper Le Journal du Dimanche in which Cooperation Minister Jacques Godfrain said that the force, which France pressed the world to create, was no longer viable.
"It's now out of the question (for the force to be deployed)," Godfrain said.

Until his interview, France's position was that Paris still backed the idea of a multinational force commanded by a Canadian general and aimed at deploying in anarchic eastern Zaire to ensure aid reached refugees from neighbouring Rwanda and displaced Zaireans.

The force has been unable to get off the ground due to opposition from the Kinshasa government and Rwandan-backed rebels, as well as because of apparent lack of enthusiasm by some contributor countries when hundreds of thousands of refugees began heading home.
Godfrain said in his interview that the priority now was the organisation of a conference of countries from Africa's Great Lakes region to discuss the issue.
The foreign ministry's statement recalled that France was also still attached to the idea of urgently holding such a conference.
